title: Take / took / taken
subtitle: it takes 20 minutes, take the bus, take an exam
summary: Say how long a journey or a job takes, and use the everyday phrases take an umbrella, take a photo, take an exam and take the bus.

lesson.heading: Take with time
lesson.text: We use **it takes** + person + time to say how long something needs. Alan lives near his office, so **it takes** him 20 minutes to get to work. Grace lives further away, so **it takes** her 45 minutes.

examples.text: I go to school every day. **It takes** me 30 minutes.
I do homework every day. **It took** me two hours yesterday.
*A:* How long **does it take** to get to the station? *B:* Fifteen minutes in a taxi.
*A:* How long **did it take** you to learn the Greek alphabet? *B:* A week or two.

lesson.heading: Take something with you
lesson.text: **Take** something = carry it from here to there, because you will need it.

examples.text: Are you going out? **Take** an umbrella. It's raining.
Are you going to the beach? **Take** some water with you.
Sorry, you can't **take** your camera into the museum.

lesson.heading: Take a photo, take a course, take an exam
lesson.text: We use **take** with photos and with studying. You **take a photo**, you **take a course**, you **take some lessons** and at the end you **take an exam**.

examples.text: *A:* Are you **taking** an English course? *B:* Yes. *A:* Do you have to **take** an exam? *B:* Yes, at the end of the course.
I want to **take** some Japanese lessons.

lesson.heading: Take the bus, take a taxi
lesson.text: We also use **take** with transport to say how we travel.

examples.text: *A:* How do you get to work? *B:* I **take the bus**.
In London you can **take the underground** to the London Eye.
We **took a taxi** from the airport to our hotel.
*A:* How does Nick get to work? *B:* He **takes the train**.

lesson.heading: Words that go with take
rows: take the bus / the train / the underground / a taxi
take a course / some lessons / an exam
take a photo / a photograph / a picture
take an umbrella / some water / your passport

lesson.text: Keep a page in your notebook for **take** and add every new word that goes with it (take a look at, take a chance).

exercises.prompt: At the end of the course, you have to ___.
exercises.explanation: We take an exam, we do not make an exam.

exercises.prompt: You can fly from London to Paris or you can ___.
exercises.explanation: We take the train / the bus / the underground.

exercises.prompt: You want to learn Russian? Why don't you ___?
exercises.explanation: We take a course or take lessons.

exercises.prompt: If you go out on a hot day, you need to ___ with you.
exercises.explanation: Take something with you = carry it from here to there.

exercises.prompt: Alan's office is near his house. It ___ him 20 minutes to get to work.
I did my homework yesterday. It ___ me two hours.
exercises.explanation: The past of take is took.

exercises.prompt: How long ___ it take you to learn the Greek alphabet?
exercises.explanation: We ask about the past with did it take.

exercises.prompt: Natalie walks to the station every morning and gets on the 7.40. How does she go to work? She ___.
Christopher waits at the stop outside his house every morning. How does he go to school? He ___.
You have three big bags and the airport is a long way away. How can you get there?
exercises.explanation: We take a taxi from one place to another.

exercises.prompt: What do you take with you? Match the situation with the thing.

pairs.left: You go to your English lesson.

exercises.prompt: We use take with all of these. Put each one in the right group.
Ask how long the journey to the station is.
exercises.answer: How long does it take to get to the station?
